defect_root_cause: Capacity enforcement applies LRU eviction without first purging expired entries, allowing expired data to occupy capacity and live data to be discarded. Wall-clock deadlines are also vulnerable to clock adjustments, and operations are not synchronized for concurrent callers.

eviction_analysis.eviction_strategy: LRU; successful reads and writes move the key to the most-recently-used end.
eviction_analysis.eviction_trigger: After a write, while the entry count exceeds capacity, the least-recently-used entry is removed.
eviction_analysis.expired_entry_precedence: Expired entries are not swept before capacity eviction. An expired entry is removed only when read or selected as the LRU victim, so a live LRU entry can be evicted while another expired entry remains.

boundary_case_results.case_description: A read occurs exactly at the stored expiration timestamp.
boundary_case_results.expected_behavior: The entry is treated as expired and a miss is returned.
boundary_case_results.actual_behavior: The >= check removes the entry and returns a miss.

boundary_case_results.case_description: The cache is at capacity; a non-LRU entry has expired, and the LRU entry is still live when another key is inserted.
boundary_case_results.expected_behavior: Remove the expired entry before evicting any live entry.
boundary_case_results.actual_behavior: The capacity loop removes the LRU entry without checking expiration, leaving the expired entry in the cache.

boundary_case_results.case_description: The system wall clock moves backward after an entry is written.
boundary_case_results.expected_behavior: Elapsed TTL should not be extended by a wall-clock adjustment.
boundary_case_results.actual_behavior: The deadline comparison uses time.time(), so a backward adjustment can delay expiration.

ttl_expiration_analysis.ttl_value_or_source: The constructor defaults to a fixed 5-second TTL for each write.
ttl_expiration_analysis.expiration_basis: Absolute expiration timestamp computed from the write time using time.time(). Reads do not extend the deadline.
ttl_expiration_analysis.boundary_operator: time.time() >= expires_at; an entry is expired at the deadline itself.

entry_lifecycle_analysis.lifecycle_summary: A write stores a value and an absolute deadline, replacing any prior value for the key. A successful read updates LRU order. Reads delete an expired requested entry; capacity pressure removes the LRU entry, whether or not it has expired.
entry_lifecycle_analysis.expiration_cleanup_behavior: Lazy cleanup on reads, with no background sweep. Capacity eviction does not proactively identify expired entries.

distributed_cache_risk_analysis.risk_summary: Wall-clock differences or adjustments can cause nodes to disagree about expiration. The implementation has no synchronization or cross-node coordination, so replicated copies can also diverge in contents and eviction order.
distributed_cache_risk_analysis.affected_scenario: Two nodes store the same key at different local times, or a local clock moves backward while reads and writes continue; concurrent operations on one instance can also interleave without protection.
